title: Banded zoom anchor and screenreader succinct mode for high-density time-series
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: High-density time-series (hundreds+ series or long time windows) causes heavy DOM churn for legends/tooltips and long, noisy screenreader output. Mobile and low-power devices experience jank due to many interactive nodes.

Goal: Introduce a compact interaction pattern composed of two complementary pieces: (1) a banded zoom anchor (visual + touch/keyboard affordance) that lets users set and refine focused ranges without instantiating full per-series tooltips, and (2) a screenreader succinct mode that collapses legend and tooltip content into a short, contextual summary optimized for navigational use and regression testing. Ensure these patterns map to design tokens, respect motion-reduce preferences, and fall back to existing behaviors on large-screen/desktop where full detail is desired.

Scope: design system tokens (color bands, spacing, token names), component behaviors for Chart, Legend, Tooltip, Minimap; accessibility copy and aria patterns; interaction specs for touch/keyboard; handoff artifacts for engineering (props, CSS variables, accessibility checklist).

Non-goal: Replacing the full tooltip/legend experience for desktop power users — this is an adaptive mode for high-density or constrained contexts.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates banded zoom anchor interaction for desktop and mobile with reduced DOM states
Screenreader succinct mode reduces per-interaction announcement length to <= 240 characters and passes VoiceOver/JAWS smoke tests
Performance: initial render + interaction (touch drag to set band) stays within 60ms main-thread budget on a mid-tier mobile CPU (profile attached)
Design tokens for band colors and spacing added to tokens.json with semantic names (chart.band.*), and engineers confirm mapping
QA checklist with keyboard-only navigation and no keyboard trap; automated e2e regression created (screenshot + SR assertion)
Engineering PR merges with unit tests and storybook entries for both 'succinct' and 'expanded' modes
design_notes: Banded zoom anchor: a semi-opaque band overlay shown above the minimap that can be dragged/resized. Use subtle inset shadow for affordance; reduce animation in motion-preference mode.
Interaction states: collapsed (overview), active-drag, committed-range. While dragging, suspend per-point hover tooltips; show a single micro-summary overlay tied to the band center.

Succinct SR mode: when activated (auto for >N series or toggle in chart menu), compute a summary: 'Showing 12 series; focus 1h window from 2026-03-01 10:00 — mean 3.2, peak 9.1 on series A'. Announce via aria-live="polite" and provide a keyboard shortcut to step through top 3 series details.
Tokens: introduce chart.band.fill, chart.band.stroke, chart.band-grip-size, chart.succinct-font-size; prefer CSS variables so runtime teams can toggle themes without rebuilds.

Legend condensation: in succinct mode, collapse legend rows into a single summarizer line with expand-on-demand. Keep color swatches in DOM but lazy-render metadata (min/max/last) to avoid costly layouts.
Performance: off-main canvas render for series lines; only sync minimal DOM nodes (band grips, summarizer). Provide a fall-back to canvas-only rendering on low-memory devices.
Testing: create synthetic high-density dataset (>=300 series) for perf runs; add storybook 'succinct-mode' with knobs for series count and sequence length.
Localization: ensure succinct strings have variable placeholders and support truncation rules; coordinate with i18n for short locale variants.
decisions: Use aria-live='polite' for banded-range announcements to avoid interrupting screen reader flows
Succinct mode will be auto-enabled for chart instances with series_count >= 75 and window_width <= 720px, configurable via prop
Use CSS variables for token surface to allow runtime theme toggles; token naming aligned with existing chart.* namespace
Tooltip suppression during band drag to reduce DOM thrash; show single micro-summary overlay instead
Provide an explicit toggle in the chart settings to force 'expanded' mode for users who prefer full legends
tradeoffs: Reduced verbosity for SR users may hide fine-grained per-series anomalies — mitigated by keyboard step-through for top series
Auto-enabling succinct mode risks surprising desktop users on small windows; mitigated by clear setting and persisted preference
Relying on off-main canvas reduces DOM overhead but makes ink-level interactions (hover per-point) more expensive to implement; we limit those in succinct mode
Adding tokens increases surface area for design-system maintenance; kept to a small semantic set to balance flexibility and complexity

comments: 2026-02-19 Maya Chen: Initial concept sketch uploaded to Figma. Goal is to reduce SR noise and improve band-based exploration. Posted to #design-charts for feedback.
2026-02-22 Liam O'Neill: Sync with Runtime team — they recommend limiting DOM updates during drag and exposing a 'succinct' prop to the JS SDK. Asked Eng to prototype canvas fallback. (See PR draft)
2026-02-26 Priya Rao (engineering): Prototype band grips implemented in paper branch; observed 30% drop in main-thread during drag using canvas + single overlay. Pushed benchmark to perf dashboard.
2026-03-03 Kira Patel (a11y): Reviewed ARIA approach. Suggested using role='region' with aria-label for band summary and explicit keyboard shortcut documentation. Minor copy tweaks suggested.

2026-03-08 Design review notes: PM asked for analytics events: 'succinct_mode_enabled', 'band_commit', 'band_resize' to help evaluate usage. Agreed to persist user preference in localStorage and surface in account settings in a later follow-up.
